messages:
Maria Gonzalez: Heads-up — I prototyped a default fallback routing flow for alerts when primary channels fail. Posting screenshots in the Drive after this.
AJ Park: Nice. What's the priority order logic? region? channel type? :thinking:
Maria Gonzalez: MVP: user-configured list (order), then channel-type preference (pager > sms > email), then region affinity. But we should let teams pin a fallback policy too.
Ben Wallace: Love pinning. UX question: do we expose 'channel-type preference' as a dropdown or a condensed pill UI? Dropdown is clearer but pill is compact.
Dena Li: Pill with a tooltip sounds good for density. But keyboard nav needs to be explicit — arrows to reorder.
Maria Gonzalez: Good call — reordering is the main interaction. I mocked a small drag handle + number ordering that falls back to keyboard reorder (up/down).
AJ Park: Can you paste the minimal policy JSON we plan to save? helps infra align.
Maria Gonzalez: Sure:
```
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "order": ["pagerduty", "sms", "slack_channel", "email"],
    "pin_for_team": false,
    "region_affinity": true
  }
}
```
Kai: Quick accessibility nit: the drag handle alone is tough for screen reader users. Make the list items have an explicit "move up / move down" button and aria-live updates.
Dena Li: +1. Also add an aria-label that reads the channel type and its priority position.
Ben Wallace: Copy question: current label "Fallback channel order" feels clunky. Alternatives: "Fallback routing", "Alternate escalation order", "If primary unreachable". Thoughts?
AJ Park: I prefer short: "Fallback routing". Clear and matches infra docs.
Maria Gonzalez: I'm leaning "Alternate escalation order" because it's slightly more explicit for non-SRE folks. But maybe we can show both: label + microcopy under it.
Dena Li: Microcopy idea: "Used when a higher-priority channel does not acknowledge the alert within X minutes or is unavailable." Keep X configurable.
Ben Wallace: On the preview — we need a simulated timeline in the preview pane showing a faux alert moving through the list with timings. Helps teams understand.
Maria Gonzalez: I built a small animated preview that steps through channels and shows color-coded outcomes (delivered, failed, acknowledged). I'll upload the GIF.
Kai: For timezones: suppression windows should be team-localized. If team A is in UTC-7 and team B in UTC+1, preview should render local times and a global banner that says what timezone the policy applies to.
AJ Park: +1. And allow a checkbox "Apply policy to all team members' local timezones" vs fixed timezone.
Dena Li: Edge case: recurring suppression (weekend maintenance) + timezone changes (DST). Need to define semantics: we should store as wall-clock local times with tz offset metadata.
Ben Wallace: UI question: when a team pins a fallback policy at org-level, should the per-route setting show "org-locked" and a link to override? I think show locked badge and a read-only preview with an "Request change" CTA.
Maria Gonzalez: I'll mock the locked state. Also thinking about an inline diff view when someone changes the org fallback so route owners can see what's different.
design-bot: Reminder — design critique tomorrow 11am PT. Add any final mocks to the drive by EOD.
AJ Park: Couple of tiny copy tweaks to propose: change "Used when" -> "Applies when", and "pin for team" -> "Pin at org level". Shorter.
Dena Li: Agree. Also for the microcopy about acknowledgement, be explicit about what counts as "acknowledged" (any manual ack in pager or a slack thread reply?). Clarify in help text.
Maria Gonzalez: Will do. I'll iterate mocks: update label to "Fallback routing" on the main screen but include microcopy: "Alternate escalation order. Applies when higher-priority channels are unavailable or don't acknowledge within X minutes."
Ben Wallace: One last UX nudge: show an inline cost estimate per policy (SMS costs) so teams can see unit economics when preferring SMS over Slack. Tiny $ icon with tooltip.
Kai: Love that. Also ensure color contrast in the preview statuses meets AA (red/green combos — don't rely on color alone).
Maria Gonzalez: All great — I'll upload updated artboards + a11y checklist. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
AJ Park: Thanks — will bring infra questions to the critique.
Dena Li: And I'll draft the keyboard/aria flows for the reorder interaction.
Maria Gonzalez: ✅ putting everything in the drive link now: https://drive.redwood/design/fallback-routing-mockups
Ben Wallace: LGTM
Maria Gonzalez: Closing thread for now. If you have tiny nits after review, drop them on the doc.
